title: Time constants and phase angle
blurb: Work out RC time constants, the phase angle of series RLC circuits, and convert impedance to admittance.

E5B01.why: In one **time constant** (τ = R × C) a capacitor reaches 63.2% of the applied voltage, or falls to 36.8% when discharging.

E5B02.why: Susceptance is the imaginary part of admittance and uses the letter **B**.
E5B02.trap: Y is admittance, G is conductance, X is reactance.

E5B03.why: Admittance is 1 ÷ Z: take the **reciprocal of the magnitude** and **change the sign of the angle**. 50∠30° gives 0.02∠−30°.

E5B04.trap: Don't treat the capacitors as series (they would halve) or use one part alone.

E5B05.why: Admittance is the reciprocal of impedance, so for pure reactance susceptance is **1 ÷ X** in size (the sign flips, since 1 ÷ jX = −j ÷ X).

E5B06.why: Admittance Y = G + jB. Susceptance **B** is its imaginary part, as reactance is for impedance.

E5B07.why: XL − XC = 250 − 500 = −250. θ = arctan(−250 ÷ 1000) = **−14.0°**: net capacitive, so voltage lags current.
E5B07.trap: Voltage leads only when XL is larger. Here XC (500) beats XL (250), so voltage lags.

E5B08.why: XL − XC = 100 − 300 = −200. θ = arctan(−200 ÷ 100) = **−63°**: net capacitive, voltage lags.

E5B09.why: In a capacitor **current leads voltage by 90°** (ELI the ICE man: I before E in C).
E5B09.trap: Voltage leading current by 90° is the inductor.

E5B10.why: In an inductor **voltage leads current by 90°** (ELI: E before I in L).
E5B10.trap: Current leading voltage is the capacitor.

E5B11.why: XL − XC = 75 − 25 = +50. θ = arctan(50 ÷ 100) = **+27°**: net inductive, voltage leads current.

E5B12.why: Admittance (Y) is the **inverse of impedance**, Y = 1 ÷ Z, measured in siemens.
E5B12.trap: The inverse of reactance alone is susceptance, not admittance.
